material_blockers.bounded_resolution: Retain v1 and close the phase lifetime table in a separate addendum: live canonical records versus immutable candidate/terminal outputs; exact in-memory versus streamed artifact retention; bounded transient/snapshot/section-reader storage; consumer evidence and provenance/refusal rules; path-pool ownership if final paths are reconstructed only from retained query frames. Keep physical writer/readback and their call reservations explicitly pending. Do not silently lift capture caps or substitute a digest/ready flag for bytes.
material_blockers.observation: The output reservation includes separate candidate and terminal ledgers, while the named retained payload sum includes one canonical evidence table. The design does not yet close the exact lifetime/provenance of frozen candidate bytes, final terminal bytes and checker access while canonical facts change, or the maximum active hash/slice transient.
material_blockers.scope_limit: No RSS, timing, physical I/O or full-roster claim is requested. This is one representation/lifetime closure within the existing proposal, not a new runtime framework or feature family.
material_blockers.why_material: Each maximum ledger exceeds the proposed captured-file cap. Two ledgers plus the child reservation exceed the proposed captured-total cap. Full artifact capture therefore cannot be presumed. Conversely, a manifest or iterator over mutable records is not immutable captured byte evidence. The 60,208,650 figure is a named retained encoded-payload sum, not a complete phase peak or checker-storage proof.
